old: consisted of such travel books
new: consisted of histories of voyages of discovery
reason: Source: 'a history of all the voyages made for purposes of discovery composed the whole of our good Uncle Thomas' library'; 'such' narrows it to the polar/North Pacific accounts just mentioned.

old: when lack of exercise lets the blood practically freeze in your veins
new: when no exercise keeps the blood from actually freezing in your veins
reason: Source: 'when no exercise prevents the blood from actually freezing in your veins'; 'practically' softens a literal danger into hyperbole.

old: I asked my father for a few weeks' reprieve.
new: I obtained a few weeks' reprieve from my father.
reason: Source: 'I obtained from my father a respite of some weeks'; candidate says only that he asked, not that it was granted.

old: but I broke free
new: but I escaped
reason: Source: 'one hand was stretched out, seemingly to detain me, but I escaped'; 'broke free' implies the creature actually seized him.

old: impossible to touch or see through
new: blocking both my touch and my sight
reason: Source 'impervious to my touch or sight' means the bodies were obstacles his touch and sight could not pass; 'impossible to touch' (the natural aural parse) says he could not touch them at all, contradicting the next sentence about obstacles.

old: like his morrow
new: like his tomorrow
reason: Quoted verse was partially modernized (ne'er/Nought) but 'morrow' remains an archaic island; protocol asks verse to be modernized like prose.

old: I had a persistent feeling
new: I had a vague feeling
reason: Source 'an obscure feeling' = dim/indistinct, not persistent.

old: the monster would commit
new: the monster I had created would commit
reason: Source 'the monster whom I had created'; the clause of self-accusation is dropped.

old: the spectators' certainty of the monstrous crime
new: the spectators' imagining of the monstrous crime
reason: Source 'by the imagination of the enormity she was supposed to have committed' - the mental picture of the crime, not a stated certainty.

old: With a few melancholy words,
new: Making a few melancholy sounds,
reason: Source 'Uttering a few sounds' deliberately reflects the Creature's pre-linguistic perception (he learns these are words only in the next chapter; 15.16 keeps 'sounds').

old: Then he spoke a few words,
new: Then he uttered a few sounds,
reason: Source 'he then pronounced a few sounds' - same pre-linguistic perspective as above.

old: the Jura, and the Alps
new: the Juras, and the Alps
reason: Source prints 'the Juras'; proper nouns reproduced as printed (non-blocking; 11.23 and 11.27 'Jura' singular elsewhere follow source).

old: But a creature as deformed and horrible as myself wouldn't refuse me.
new: But a creature as deformed and horrible as myself wouldn't deny herself to me.
reason: Source 'one as deformed and horrible as myself would not deny herself to me' — the pronoun 'herself' is the first signal that the companion is female; candidate drops the gender entirely. [lead: more natural verb, keeps source "deny herself"]

old: St. Andrews
new: St. Andrew's
reason: Source prints 'St. Andrew's'; candidate silently standardizes the proper noun (other source spellings like Coupar, Strasburgh, Chamounix are kept).

old: I was also cursed with a hideously
new: I was also endowed with a hideously
reason: Source 'I was, besides, endued with a figure'; 'cursed' adds a judgment the source leaves ironic/neutral.

old: were blows too bitter and final to bear
new: were misfortunes more bitter and irreparable
reason: Source 'misfortunes more bitter and irreparable' (a comparison with poverty); 'too ... to bear' adds a claim he could not bear them.

old: and that the French government might seize him at any moment
new: and that he would soon be handed over to the French government
reason: Source 'he should speedily be delivered up to the French government' — expected soon, by handover; candidate weakens to 'might' and changes the mechanism to French seizure.

old: during my usual trip to the woods to gather food and firewood,
new: during my usual trip to the woods to gather my own food and bring home firewood for my protectors,
reason: Source 'where I collected my own food and brought home firing for my protectors' — the secret kindness to the cottagers (later invoked in 19.27) is dropped.

old: They weren't rich,
new: They didn't seem rich,
reason: Source hedges: 'They did not appear rich'; candidate states it as fact.

old: I felt emotions of gentleness and pleasure that had long seemed dead.
new: I felt emotions of gentleness and pleasure that had long seemed dead revive within me.
reason: Source 'emotions ... that had long appeared dead, revive within me'; the revival is dropped.

old: Your violent impulses will be renewed.
new: Your evil passions will be renewed.
reason: Source 'your evil passions will be renewed'; 'violent impulses' drops the moral judgment Victor makes.

old: My violent impulses will disappear,
new: My evil passions will have fled,
reason: Source 'My evil passions will have fled' — the Creature echoes Victor's phrase; keep the echo and the moral term.

old: Since I couldn't sympathize with him, I had no right
new: I thought that since I couldn't sympathize with him, I had no right
reason: Source 'I thought that as I could not sympathise with him, I had no right' — Victor's reasoning at the time, not a narratorial assertion.

old: Now I truly exist!
new: Now I enjoy existence!
reason: Source 'now I enjoy existence!'; 'truly exist' changes the claim.

old: at the first real test of your courage — or if you prefer, the first mighty, terrifying trial —
new: at the first imagined danger — or, if you prefer, the first mighty, terrifying trial of your courage —
reason: Source: 'with the first imagination of danger, or, if you will, the first mighty and terrific trial of your courage' — Frankenstein taunts that the danger is merely imagined; 'first real test' inverts that and drops the first of the two alternatives. [lead: "imagined" keeps the source taunt that the danger is only imagined]

old: A race of monsters
new: A race of devils
reason: Source: 'a race of devils would be propagated' — Victor's diabolical term for the creatures' offspring flattened to 'monsters'.

old: between me and civilization
new: between me and my fellow human beings
reason: Source: 'an insuperable barrier between me and my fellow creatures' — about people, not civilization.

old: all left behind, all at the monster's mercy.
new: all left behind, on whom the monster might now satisfy his bloodthirsty, merciless passions.
reason: Source: 'on whom the monster might satisfy his sanguinary and merciless passions' — the bloodthirst is dropped. [lead: "satisfy" instead of archaic "sate"]

old: — though I was less innocent than poor Justine had been.
new: — I, who was less innocent than poor Justine had been.
reason: Source: 'suffer the penalty of the law, less innocent than poor Justine had been'; 'though' sets up a contrast that makes the sentence illogical when heard.

old: would travel by boat that night to Evian and continue our journey the next day
new: would set out by boat, spend that night at Evian, and continue our journey the next day
reason: Source: 'commence our journey by water, sleeping that night at Evian' — they sail by day (next paragraphs); candidate implies a night voyage.

old: with all the fierce devotion a man feels
new: with all the devotion a man feels
reason: Source: 'all that affection which a man feels' — 'fierce' is not in the source.

old: from the blue seas of the south
new: from the blue seasons of the south
reason: Source prints 'blue seasons of the south'; 'seas' silently corrects the source text (RULES: do not silently correct).

old: after they'd barely survived these
new: after they had, with luck, survived these
reason: Source: 'after they might happily have surmounted this' — 'happily' = fortunately, and the survival is conditional; 'barely' shifts the sense.

old: what can I say about the loss of this extraordinary spirit?
new: what can I say about the untimely death of this glorious spirit?
reason: Source: 'the untimely extinction of this glorious spirit' — 'untimely' dropped.
